content: Indication-specific dosing for star anise (Illicium verum), also known as aniseed stars, badiana, or Chinese anise, has not been established as safe or effective. There is no proven standard dose for this substance. Star anise has been traditionally used for various conditions, including respiratory infections, inflammation, influenza (the flu), swine flu, avian flu, gastrointestinal upset, flatulence, loss of appetite, infant colic, cough, and bronchitis. However, more research is required to evaluate its efficacy for these indications. While star anise is used in the production of oseltamivir (Tamiflu), it does not possess any proven antiviral activity on its own. It is important to note that star anise should not be confused with Japanese star anise, a smaller and toxic variety. Repeated use of star anise may lead to the development of sensitivity in some individuals. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, there is no specific categorization or data available (Pregnancy Category: N/A; Lactation: N/A). However, substances classified as A are generally considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
